page.summary: Find and cleanse a totem when removing a live Hex or converting that cleanse into a useful heal or repair window repays the search time.

verdict.recommendation: Treat cleansing as a response to a visible threat or a planned reward, not a standing detour from repairs.
verdict.soloQ: Follow nearby totem information and abandon a long search when a rescue or useful repair is available.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Tell teammates which Hex or cleanse reward is worth pursuing so several players do not duplicate the same search.
verdict.mainWeakness: Search and cleanse time can buy nothing against a low-totem match and can consume a totem a teammate wanted to bless.

options.whyItsHere: Shows nearby totems during an already useful route; use it to shorten a search rather than roam solely for a distant dull totem.
Rewards consecutive cleanses with faster cleansing and a farthest-totem lead; useful when several totems really need removal.
Turns a cleanse into a later locker self-heal, provided the user is not Broken and can take a safe locker pause.
Converts a cleanse into repair speed until the next lost health state; strongest reason to cleanse when safe repair time follows.

weaknesses: Totems are finite and searching competes with generator, rescue and teammate Boon time.
commonMistakes: Leaving a live objective to clear every dull totem without a reward or Hex to answer.
Expecting Inner Strength from blessing instead of cleansing, or trying its locker heal while Broken.
Keeping a cleanse reward plan after the next health-state loss ends Overzealous.

opening: Decide whether the immediate job is removing a dangerous Hex or earning a specific cleanse reward; check what objective or rescue the detour will delay.

rows.situation: A relevant Hex is active and a totem is on a reachable route.
rows.action: Use Small Game's nearby reveal to check that route and cleanse the target if the removal matters now; stop ranging outward when the team needs a rescue or generator completion.
rows.why: The threat makes the detour valuable, while a broad hunt can surrender more tempo than the Hex costs.

rows.situation: Another totem removal is justified after your first cleanse.
rows.action: Use Counterforce's farthest-totem reveal as a lead only if a second cleanse is worth its travel; otherwise return to the team objective.
rows.why: Its speed and information improve a real cleanse chain but cannot make an unnecessary chain valuable.

rows.situation: A safe dull or Hex totem is nearby and a later self-heal or uninterrupted repair period is likely.
rows.action: Cleanse for Inner Strength's locker heal or Overzealous's repair bonus, then take that planned follow-up; skip the totem if the follow-up is unlikely.
rows.why: The payoff comes after cleansing and still requires a usable locker or repair window.

rows.situation: No meaningful Hex remains, the team needs an immediate save, or a teammate is using the totem for a Boon.
rows.action: Leave the totem and resume rescue or repair; coordinate before consuming a planned Boon site.
rows.why: A finite totem can be worth more as team time or a shared zone than as an isolated cleanse.

abortWhen: Stop hunting when no Hex or near-term cleanse reward justifies another travel and cleanse cycle.
Yield to an urgent rescue or a teammate's planned Boon site rather than finishing a low-value search.
